title: Cover GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS on the integrity security axis (BEFORE/AFTER/RACE arms)
description:
FILED BY worker-b8af1a87 from task-e3d5fd057ca24d50a973cb61e4911f5f, which DECLARED the boundary and disclosed this red rather than hiding it. QA's reject on that task said explicitly: "Do NOT delete the roster entry to quiet (3); that hides a real boundary" and "file the follow-up for the 3 arms. Keep the entry."

MEASURED RED, verbatim, reproduced at HEAD by `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts` (run it directly: `pnpm test:security` dies earlier on a FOREIGN TS6133 before vitest starts):

  FAIL  integrity-boundaries.security.ts > integrity axis versus the declared-boundary roster > reads a positive number of integrity entries off the roster
  AssertionError: expected [ ...(14) ] to have a length of 13 but got 14
   at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:106:30

  FAIL  ... > covers every integrity boundary the roster declares (roster minus covered is empty)
  AssertionError: expected [ 'GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS' ] to deeply equal []
   at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:111:75

  FAIL  ... > generates a positive, three-armed case count for GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS
  AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 0
   at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:124:27

  Test Files  1 failed | 8 passed (9) / Tests  3 failed | 476 passed (479)

CAUSE, stated plainly: task-e3d5fd05 added the roster entry `{ constant: "GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS", file: "packages/scheduler/src/graph-content-issues.ts", axis: "integrity" }` at tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts:199. Rostering a boundary ACTIVATES a closed coverage ratchet in the axis slice: integrity-boundaries.security.ts parses the roster's committed bytes for its own axis tag and demands BEFORE, AFTER and RACE hostile arms per constant. There is no quiet tag — retagging to `scheduler-activation` was measured and moves the same three failures to that slice.

WORK: add BEFORE/AFTER/RACE hostile arms for GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS in the integrity axis's hostile-cases module, following the shape the sibling arms already use (each forgery arm RE-SEALS through production and carries an `integrity` thunk asserted ok:true first), and bump the pinned integrity cardinality 13 -> 14 at integrity-boundaries.security.ts:106 plus EXPECTED_ROSTER_SIZE / EXPECTED_DISTRIBUTION in the roster if they also moved.

SUBJECT UNDER TEST, already landed and green: packages/scheduler/src/graph-content-issues.ts (GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS = GRAPH_CONTENT_CODEC | GRAPH_CONTENT_IDENTITY | GRAPH_VALIDATION), the codec in graph-content.ts / graph-content-fields.ts / graph-content-format.ts, and `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` = Test Files 45 passed / Tests 1411 passed.

DO NOT close this by deleting the roster entry.
definitionOfDone: tests/security/integrity-boundaries.security.ts reports GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS as covered: roster-minus-covered is empty and armsFor("GRAPH_CONTENT_LAYERS") contains BEFORE, AFTER and RACE with a nonzero asserted case count.
The pinned integrity roster cardinality is corrected to the true count (13 -> 14) and any sibling cardinality assertion that moved with it, with no roster entry deleted or retagged to a quieter axis.

Each new hostile arm re-seals through the production codec (encodeGraphContent / decodeGraphContent) rather than a test-local reimplementation, and asserts the exact GRAPH_CONTENT_* code and layer it expects, never merely that the operation failed.
`npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts` exits 0 with a nonzero Test Files count line, and a mutation drill on one new arm makes a NAMED test go red on its own assertion.
